Variants.Content: The Staunton family is based on Crow's Roost and is an ancient vassal on the northern shore of the king's territory facing Blackwater Bay. The coastal location of Crow's Roost allows Staunton to face farmland, fishing grounds, coastal waterways and the King's Landing at the same time; the prosperity of the royal realm can bring markets to the town, and royal wars can also allow fleets and levies to arrive first. The Staunton family name was linked to the view of Blackwater Bay from Crow's Roost, and the lord had to constantly carry messages between court, the coast and local villages. For sailors, the castle is a beacon; for farmers, it is a tax collector and protector; for the royal family, it is a window on the periphery of the capital.

The royal nobles regarded Staunton as a coastal vassal who could not be ignored outside the Red Castle. Crow's Roost Castle is close enough to King's Landing to hear orders quickly, and close enough to the sea to see danger quickly. This position brings honor, but also a responsibility that cannot be shied away from.

People near Crow's Roost watch the tide, boats, and tax trucks. Merchants benefited when ports were opened, fishing nets were folded when fleets appeared, and farmers handed over grain when royal levies were issued. Word of Staunton's good and bad always spread quickly to both sides of the bay.
